elements.name: question15
elements.html:
The current study is evaluating a drug developed to treat high blood pressure. When left uncontrolled, high blood pressure can place significant strain on the body over time, increasing the risk of various cardiovascular complications, including heart disease and stroke. 

 

As this is a Phase 1 trial, the primary objectives are to evaluate the safety and tolerability of the study drug and to understand how the drug behaves in the body. 

 

Later parts of this study will also involve an investigational medication developed to lower “bad” cholesterol levels (LDL-C). For that reason, participants within both parts of the study will undergo a pre-screening test of their LDL-C levels to ensure they fit the study criteria.

elements.name: question16
elements.html:
Study Drug

 

Participants will be randomly allocated to receive either the study drug or a placebo. Allocation will be done double-blinded meaning neither yourself nor the study team will know which group you are in until after the study has finished.

 

Participants will receive either the study drug or placebo in a 4:1 ratio. 

 

Both the study drug and placebo will be administered as a subcutaneous injection, which is an injection done into the fatty tissue in your torso area.

elements.name: question49
elements.html:
Schedule

 

Pre-screening visit length: 1 hr

 

Overall, participation in this study lasts roughly 1 year.

 

The study begins with a pre-screening visit where you will attend the site for a blood test to assess your cholesterol (LDL-C) levels. If your levels are within the criteria for this study, you will be brought back to site for a screening visit which will involve a more comprehensive medical check. There is a small chance that the site will be able to conduct your pre-screening and screening visit on the same day, but this will be dependent on doctor's availability and is unlikely.  

 

If you pass the screening visit, your next visit will involve an 3-night in-clinic stay. Participants will be randomly allocated to receive either the study drug or a placebo once, as a subcutaneous injection. This will be done on Day 1 of your stay, after the first night. 

 

Following discharge, you will have a total of 14 follow-up visits. These will be approximately as follows:

 

  • 5 days after the in-clinic stay (D8)
  • 1 week after (D15)
  • Approx 2 weeks after (D30)
  • Every 30 days after for 11 visits until D360

 

ABPM

As part of this study, you will undergo ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) at 3 points. ABPM is a 24-hour test that automatically measures and records your BP throughout your normal daily routine and sleep. It involves wearing a compact recorder on a belt or shoulder strap that is connected to a BP cuff on your upper arm. This cuff will automatically take BP readings every 30 mins throughout the 24 hours. 

 

ABPM will occur:

  • Between 6-1 days before admission (D-7 - D-2)
  • D30
  • D180

 

Cohort A1 ROC 

 

Your in-clinic stay will be from the 10th - 13th of December.

 

You would then return to the clinic for follow-up appointments on the 18th and 25th of December (±1 day), 9th of January (±2 days), 8th of February (±3 days), 10th of March (±3 days), 9th of April (±7 days), 9th of May (±7 days), 8th of June (±7 days), 8th of July (±7 days), 7th of August (±7 days), 6th of September (±7 days), 6th of October (±7 days), 5th of November (±7 days) and the 5th of December (±7 days).

 

Cohort A2 Sentinel 

 

Your in-clinic stay will be from the 21st - 24th of January.

 

You would then return to the clinic for follow-up appointments on the 29th of January, the 5th (±1 day) and 20th of February (±2 days), 22nd of March (±3 days), 21st of April (±3 days), 21st of May (±7 days), 20th of June (±7 days), 20th of July (±7 days), 19th of August (±7 days), 18th of September (±7 days), 18th of October (±7 days), 17th of November (±7 days), 17th of December (±7 days) and the 16th of January (±7 days).

elements.name: question17
elements.html:
Reimbursement

 

You will be reimbursed for your participation in the study. The payment is broken down as follows:

 

  • $200 for the pre-screening visit,
  • $300 for the screening visit,
  • $300 for your admission and discharge days
  • $600 for each night you stay in the clinic,
  • $300 for each follow-up visit,
  • $200 for any visits required to pick up the ABPM,
  • $1000 retention bonus at the end of the study, if all required study visits are attended,
  • $600 if you are an eligible Alternate. An Alternate is someone who is enrolled in case they are needed but does not receive the treatment.

 

If you attend all required visits, your total reimbursement will be approx. $7,300.

elements.name: question1
elements.html:
If the PT is taking any prescription medications daily they are not suitable (contraception is okay). 

 

There is no specific wash out required for prescription medications (except for the ones listed below). But remember, PT's should not come off their prescription medications to join a study! Stopping medication must only be done after speaking to a medical professional.

 

Permitted medications 

  • Contraceptives (daily use is okay)
  • Vitamins/multivitamins at standard doses (daily use is okay)
  • Protein powders and creatine at standard doses (that don't contain active herbal or medicinal ingredients) (daily use is okay)

 

Use of the below medications up to 3 times a week is okay. Any higher frequency, pls raise doctor enquiry

  • Paracetamol/ibuprofen
  • OTC antihistamines 
  • Low-potency OTC corticosteroid creams (eg. hydrocortisone)
  • Very occasional Ventolin
  • Nasal corticosteroids or decongestants
  • Pantoprazole (Somac) or Esomeprazole (Nexium)
  • OTC topical antifungals
  • OTC cold and flu medicines

 

For any other infrequently used prescription medication pls raise a medical enquiry ⚠️

 

Exclusionary medications if taken within 30 days of screening:

 

Any medication, herbal supplement, or nutraceutical known to reduce blood pressure or serum lipids

 

Examples of medications for high blood pressure:

  • Perindopril, Ramipril, Lisinopril, Enalapril
  • Candesartan, Telmisartan, Irbesartan, Losartan, Valsartan
  • Amlodipine, Lercanidipine, Diltiazem, Felodipine
  • Indapamide, Hydrochlorothiazide, Chlorthalidone, Frusemide
  • Metoprolol, Bisoprolol, Atenolol, Carvedilol

 

Examples of medications for lipids/cholesterol:

  • Rosuvastatin, Atorvastatin, Simvastatin, Pravastatin, Fluvastatin, Pitavastatin
  • Ezetimibe
  • Evolocumab
  • Alirocumab
  • Bempedoic acid
  • Fenofibrate, Gemfibrozil
  • Niacin
  • Red yeast rise
  • Fish oil (high doses only)

elements.title: Before we wrap up, I’d like to share details about our referral program. If you refer someone to us you can receive up to $250 if they enrol and participate in the study. Would you like to hear more?

elements.name: question21
elements.html:
Great! Here's how it works:

 

To refer someone, you will need to provide them with a unique referral ID. The person you refer will need to provide us this ID either when they sign up on our website, or when they speak to us over the phone. This ID is essential, as it ensures we can track and reimburse you for any referrals.

 

For each person you refer who comes in for an in-person screening visit, you'll receive $50. If they go on to enrol and participate in the study, you'll earn an additional $200.

 

There's no limit- you can refer as many people as you'd like, as long as you have an exisiting relationship with them. It's important to note that you cannot advertise for referrals. This program is based on personal connections, so please only refer people you know.

 

If you're interested, we can set up your Unique Referral ID today if you would like (the unique referral ID is REF[p number]. E.g., REFP14471)

 

Who do you know you might be interested in this trial? (if they don't know anyone for this trial, they can also refer someone to any other trial)

 

Would you like us to send you an email that you can forward on to them?
